title: Admin Holster: Shortflows & Ops Automation
creator: Lena Park
description: Create 'Admin Holster' — a curated, lightweight library of short, composable administrative flows (shortflows) that expose common remediation and diagnostics as first-class tasks. Goal is to reduce cognitive load for oncall engineers, enable secure one-click fixes for common incidents, and make runbooks reusable as atomic tasks that can be invoked from CLI, Console, or via automation. Work spans API design, safe execution primitives, RBAC/dry-run modes, and observability hooks.

notes: Design constraint: shortflows must be <120s worst-case unless explicitly marked as long-running.
Operational constraint: every shortflow invocation creates a structured audit event and stores an invocation trace for 90 days.
Implementation decision: runflows will use the existing runbook runner but expose a simplified Task API with typed inputs and a preview mode.
Fallback policy: if a shortflow fails, roll back via configured compensating action where feasible and emit high-severity incident to oncall channel.
acceptance_criteria: 5 production shortflows implemented and reviewed (restart-server, cache-prune, extend-expiry, scale-worker, rotate-keys).
CLI and Console surfaces can invoke shortflows with preview/dry-run and require RBAC checks.
Telemetry: invocation, success/failure, actor, params, and duration emitted to telemetry stream.
Automated tests cover idempotency, advisory locks, and permission gating.
Kill-switch and canary rollout mechanism in place with runbook to revert if issues are observed.
success_metrics: MTTR reduction for common incidents by 30% within 8 weeks of GA.
Oncall clicks-to-remediation reduced: median steps from 7 -> 3 for targeted flows.
At least 75% of invocations include preview/dry-run before execute in first month.
No high-severity incidents attributable to shortflow automation during canary at 10% traffic.
